_why: Scenarios for a REAL policy wording: Star Health's Arogya Sanjeevani, IRDAI's standard product.
Fetch the PDF with evals/real/fetch_policies.py; it is never committed.
Written from the policy's own wording, and every expected verdict fixed BEFORE any
run of these cases. Same author as the system, so not fully independent.
Two things differ from the synthetic sets:
1. Every payable claim on this policy is `conditional`, never `covered`: a 5%
co-payment applies to each and every claim, and this project's convention is
that a claim paid less than in full is conditional.
2. must_cite names the clause each case's `why` already named - the one that makes
the case more than a default answer - never the universal co-payment. M15 found
9 of 10 verdicts right mostly for the wrong reasons, several of them on that
co-payment, so requiring it would reward the shortcut this key exists to catch.
Empty in M15 because citation ids were then segmentation artefacts; added in M16,
once they were the policy's own clause numbers, and before any run on them.
Ids with '#' are repeats of a number (exclusion 2 is '2#2', coverage 2 is '2'),

cases.scenario: I need surgery for an inguinal hernia that was found last month. I bought this policy 14 months ago and it is my first health insurance.
cases.why: Hernia of all types is on the 24-month specified disease waiting period list (exclusion 2). Fourteen months have not served it, there was no prior cover to port, and nothing suggests an accident.

cases.scenario: I need surgery for a hernia diagnosed this year. I have held this policy for three years without a break and will be in hospital for two days.
cases.why: The 24-month specified disease waiting period (exclusion 2) is served, so hospitalisation is payable - but every claim is subject to the 5% co-payment, so it is paid less than in full.

cases.scenario: I broke my leg in a fall on a weekend trek in the hills and was admitted for three days. I am a software engineer, not a professional climber. I have held the policy four years.
cases.why: The hazardous or adventure sports exclusion (exclusion 9) applies only to participation as a professional, so an amateur's injury is not excluded. Payable, less the 5% co-payment.

cases.scenario: I had a caesarean delivery last week and was in hospital for four days. I have held the policy for five years.
cases.why: The maternity exclusion (exclusion 18) covers expenses traceable to childbirth, naming caesarean sections. There is no maternity waiting period that could have been served.

cases.scenario: I was admitted to hospital with dengue fever 20 days after buying this policy. I had no health insurance before it.
cases.why: Treatment of any illness within 30 days of the first policy commencement is excluded except for accidents (exclusion 3), and there was no earlier continuous cover to waive it.

cases.scenario: I had cataract surgery on one eye and the bill was 70,000 rupees. My sum insured is 5 lakh and I have held the policy for three years.
cases.why: The 24-month cataract waiting period is served, but cataract treatment (coverage 3) is limited to 25% of sum insured or 40,000 rupees per eye, whichever is lower - 40,000 here - before the 5% co-payment.

cases.scenario: I was admitted for pneumonia for four nights in a single room costing 8,000 rupees a night. My sum insured is 3 lakh and I have held the policy five years.
cases.why: Room rent is covered up to 2% of sum insured subject to 5,000 rupees a day (coverage 1), so 5,000 here. A room above the limit also reduces other hospital expenses proportionately, and the 5% co-payment applies. The table of benefits repeats the limit; citing only it would be a right reason this key does not accept.

cases.scenario: I was hospitalised with pneumonia while on holiday in Dubai. I have held the policy for two years.
cases.why: Treatment taken outside the geographical limits of India is excluded (exclusion 22), and all treatment must be taken in India (condition 20).

cases.scenario: Will the policy pay for cosmetic teeth whitening? I have held it for six years.
cases.why: Treatment to change appearance is excluded unless it is reconstruction after an accident, burn or cancer (exclusion 8), and dental cover is only for treatment necessitated by disease or injury.

cases.scenario: I need my gallbladder removed because of gallstones. How much of it will the policy pay?
cases.why: Calculi of the gall bladder carry a 24-month specified disease waiting period (exclusion 2), and the person has not said how long they have held the policy, so whether it is served cannot be decided.
